Q: How to change an existing user's password? A: 
vars:
myusers:
  - { name: 'user1', update_pass: 'passwd' }
  - { name: 'user2', update_pass: 'passwd' }
  - { name: 'user3', update_pass: 'passwd' } 

# Contents of passwd will be stored in ansible_facts.getent_passwd as a dict
- name: Determine local user accounts
  getent:
    database: passwd

# Update password if user account is found in /etc/passwd
- name: change passwd
  user: name={{ item.name }} password={{ item.update_pass  }} update_password=always
  with_items: myusers
  when: item in ansible_facts.getent_passwd

Q: Replace colors in PDF using ghostscript A:

I was having trouble with the gs command in OP's question, as it didn't seem to actually change the PDF. I wanted to apply this transfer function to change the document from black on white to red on black:

{1 exch sub}{0 exch sub}{0 exch sub}{1 exch sub} setcolortransfer

What I learned from the Ghostscript documentation is that setcolortransfer is deprecated in PDF 2.0, and so I'm assuming it wasn't working because the PDF viewers I was using didn't apply it anymore. What I had to do was bake in the transfer with this option:

-dTransferFunctionInfo=/Apply

Note that there are caveats with this approach, although as I only intended the PDF to be viewed on a screen it worked in my case:

The default for transfer functions is to preserve them, this is because transfer functions are a device-dependent feature, a set of transfer functions designed for an RGB device will give incorrect output on a CMYK device for instance.

Q: launch URL in Flet A: 
async def main(page: ft.Page):
    url_launcher = ft.UrlLauncher()

    async def open_repo(e):
        await url_launcher.launch_url(
            "https://github.com/iqfareez/flet-hello",
            mode=ft.LaunchMode.EXTERNAL_APPLICATION,
            web_only_window_name="_blank",
        )

    appbar = ft.AppBar(
        title=ft.Text(value="Flutter using Flet"),
        bgcolor=ft.Colors.BLUE,
        color=ft.Colors.WHITE,
        actions=[ft.IconButton(icon=ft.Icons.CODE, on_click=open_repo)])

Key differences from the old answer:

  • async def main required for async event handlers

  • ft.UrlLauncher() created in main scope replaces deprecated page.launch_url()

  • await url_launcher.launch_url(...) the method is async now

  • ft.Colors / ft.Icons capitalized (not ft.colors / ft.icons)

  • ft.run(main) replaces ft.app(target=main)

  • page.add() replaces page.controls.append() + page.update()
